evidence.fitness: Job walked: someone with a job and a side business (the sample) gets a correct 31 January figure and POA schedule, which is the core use, and the pension what-if in the taper band is correctly worth GBP 4,000 on GBP 8,000 net. A landlord with mortgage interest and dividends (a common SA profile, e.g. a company director who lets property) can be told GBP 0 tax when about GBP 1,706 is due; a landlord with small expenses is overcharged by the forced allowance; a borrower with modest interest is overcharged student loan. Scotland, HICBC and losses are disclosed exclusions, but HICBC in particular is common in SA. Usable as a first estimate for employment plus trade; not for landlords. Nearest tools: HMRC's own 'Estimate your Income Tax' and commercial SA estimators, which handle the finance cost reducer.
evidence.domain: Against GOV.UK 2025/26: personal allowance, taper, basic 37,700 and additional 125,140 bands, dividend 8.75/33.75/39.35 and GBP 500 allowance, starting rate 5,000, PSA 1,000/500/0, Class 4 6%/2% between 12,570 and 50,270, Class 2 treated as paid (pass); ordering non-savings, savings, dividends with nil-rate amounts using band space (pass); pension relief at source and Gift Aid extending both basic and additional bands and reducing ANI (pass); POA tests at GBP 1,000 and 80% at source, excluding student loan, half the relevant amount each (pass, poa.html). Departs: finance cost reducer third limb includes savings/dividends (GOV.UK: adjusted total income excludes them); property allowance election not optimised against the reducer; SA student loan income counts all unearned income instead of only when over GBP 2,000; Plan 5 charged a year early; the 'more than 80% collected at source' test uses PAYE only, ignoring other tax deducted at source (small). A CTA would accept the stacking engine and reject the landlord figures.

defects.what: Finance cost reducer's third limb uses total income including savings and dividends; GOV.UK uses adjusted total income excluding them. A landlord with rent 15,000 (expenses 2,000, mortgage interest 10,000) and 20,000 dividends is shown income tax GBP 0 where 1,706.25 is due.

Property allowance is chosen whenever it beats ordinary expenses, ignoring that it forfeits the finance cost reducer; the user cannot override. Employment 30,000, rent 10,000, expenses 500, mortgage interest 6,000 -> 5,286 instead of 4,186; GBP 1 more expense flips it (GBP 1,200 cliff).
Student loan SA income counts all savings and dividend income; GOV.UK counts unearned income only when over GBP 2,000. Employment 30,000, interest 1,500, Plan 2 -> 272.70 instead of 137.70.
Plan 5 is offered and charged for 2025/26 (employment 40,000 -> GBP 1,350), but Plan 5 repayments are not collected until April 2026; the 2025/26 employer thresholds list no Plan 5.

6 of 8 seeded mutants survive: POA 80% test, additional-rate band extension, additional dividend rate, Plan 4 threshold, Gift Aid gross-up and the finance-credit cap are untested; the one finance-cost test has no savings or dividends.

Marginal-rate finding says the next GBP 1,000 costs that much 'in tax and National Insurance' but marginalOn adds employment pay without Class 1 NIC, understating an employee's marginal rate (34.6% shown vs about 38.2% at 50,000).
Money format uses minimumFractionDigits 0, so the headline reads '£5,955.3' and '£2,456.6'.
The 80%-at-source test counts PAYE only; tax deducted at source elsewhere is not an input. The High Income Child Benefit Charge, common among SA filers, is disclosed but not modelled.

verdict: A tidy 2025/26 Self Assessment estimator whose core stacking engine is right and whose landlord and student-loan paths are not. Against GOV.UK pages fetched on 2026-11-17, the bands, taper, dividend and savings rates, PSA, starting rate, Class 4 (and Class 2 treated as paid), pension and Gift Aid band extension and the payments-on-account tests all reproduce: GBP 200,000 -> 76,203; 110,000 -> 33,432 and 29,432 with an 8,000 net pension; the worked example 10,329.50 tax and 8,932.95 due on 31 January, also on the live page. But the finance cost reducer counts dividends and savings in adjusted total income, so a landlord with dividends can be shown GBP 0 instead of 1,706.25; the property allowance is forced over the reducer (GBP 1,100 overcharge, a GBP 1,200 cliff at one pound of expense); student loan ignores the GBP 2,000 unearned-income rule; and Plan 5 is charged a year early. Tests pass 32/32 but 6 of 8 mutants survive. Disclaimer, from-memory note and exclusions are present. Does not meet the bar (correctness 2, claims 2, verification 2; median 2); finished (completeness 3). Fixable in one session: exclude savings/dividends from the ATI limb, pick the property route by total tax, apply the GBP 2,000 unearned test, drop Plan 5 for 2025/26, and add tests for each.
